prior_importants.description: `resolvesAbove` accepts a dependency found in `node_modules` folders the gate checkout never gets. These are intermediate folders, and the root's for a package with its own lockfile. In those layouts the refusal is skipped and the stage fails on a missing runner, which reads as the branch's fault.

The install command in the refusal comes from `packageManager(<repo>/<pkg.dir>)`, which only looks for a lockfile in the package's own folder. Every yarn or pnpm workspace member therefore gets told to run `npm --prefix <dir> install`, which is the wrong tool and the wrong folder.

findings.description: A nested package with no dependencies but with its own lockfile is refused on every merge, and the install the message names never clears it. It ran fine before this change.

When the nearest lockfile sits in an intermediate directory (a workspace rooted below the repo root), the code still looks only in the repo root's `node_modules` and tells the operator to install in that intermediate directory. That install can never clear the refusal. It also newly refuses a branch that used to pass.
findings.body:
**A member of a workspace rooted below the repo root gets an install command that can never clear the refusal.**

`nearestLockfile` finds the member's real workspace root, and the error message names it. The hoisting check, though, only looks in `<repoPath>/node_modules`:

```ts
const lock = nearestLockfile(repoPath, pkg.dir);
// ... of the directories above it the gate links the root's alone.
if (
  lock?.dir !== pkg.dir &&
  Object.keys(declared).every((name) => existsSync(join(repoPath, GATE_ENVIRONMENT_DIR, name)))
```

The adapter supports nested packages inside nested packages on purpose (`committedPackageDirs`, and `touchedNestedPackages`' "The innermost package owns the file", `typescript.adapter.ts:566-570`).

**Trigger:** `tools/review` is an npm or yarn-v1 workspace root, with its own `package-lock.json` and `workspaces: ["packages/*"]`. It is installed, so the dependencies of `tools/review/packages/a` are hoisted into `tools/review/node_modules`.

- A branch touching `packages/a` gives `lock.dir = 'tools/review'`. The repo root's `node_modules` lacks the deps, so the gate throws "Install it with `npm --prefix tools/review install`".
- That install is already done, so every retry is refused the same way.

**Regression:** the branch may also touch a file owned by `tools/review` itself. Before this PR, `linkEnvironment` linked `tools/review/node_modules` into the checkout, and resolution from `packages/a` walked up into it, so the stage could pass. Now the refusal loop runs before any link and blocks the merge.

**Possible direction:** check `join(repoPath, lock.dir, GATE_ENVIRONMENT_DIR, name)` and make sure the gate links `lock.dir`'s environment too. Or, if this layout is out of scope, have the advice stop naming an install that cannot help.

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/8d45bde62cd071b0f4a44b846719ff0cb202e432/src/core/merge-gate.service.ts#L1561-L1576

findings.description: The message always says "stages", even for a package whose trusted manifest declares only one of `test` or `typecheck`. Such a package gets "so its test stages cannot find their tools". Pick the singular or plural from `pkg.commands.length`.
